market.audience: age-group triathletes who want to understand performances across seasons
market.problem: Official event pages show one race at a time, making it difficult to compare splits across a career or within one distance.
market.advantage: A registered-name search gathers published full and half-distance triathlon results into a local Locker with separate split rankings, field context, free career insight and optional tips.
market.competitive_context: Event timing pages are authoritative but are organized around a single event. Training platforms generally depend on workouts or manual data; IM Iron Splits organizes published race results without an account.

proof_points.claim: The Locker and Rankings captures show split standings scoped to one race distance.
The race detail capture shows published split ranks and event-field context.
Race Book shows a free career overview and split personal bests.

story.throughline: Turn published event results into a useful private race history.

pitch.benefit: See supported results from many seasons in one locker instead of searching event pages.
pitch.problem: Timing sites show one event at a time and make it hard to revisit a whole career.
pitch.advantage: One registered-name search gathers published full and half-distance triathlon results into a local history.
pitch.proof: The literal Locker screen shows fictional, deterministic full and half-distance results gathered into one history.

pitch.benefit: Find the fastest swim, bike, run, transition and finish without mixing race types.
pitch.problem: A faster half-distance bike time can make a combined ranking meaningless beside a full-distance race.
pitch.advantage: Locker rankings keep full and half-distance results on separate lists.
pitch.proof: The literal Rankings screen shows split standings for one selected distance.

pitch.benefit: Understand a finish with official split times, division places and the race field.
pitch.problem: A finish time alone cannot show where an athlete gained time or how a split compared with the field.
pitch.advantage: Race detail keeps published splits, ranks and field percentiles beside one another.
pitch.proof: The literal race detail screen shows split times, ranks and the cached fictional event field.

frames.header: Follow your best times across seasons

pitch.benefit: See career totals, personal bests and race-by-race times without paying.
pitch.problem: Progress is difficult to read from finish times scattered across years and venues.
pitch.advantage: Race Book provides a free career overview and lets athletes inspect repeat events separately.
pitch.proof: The literal Race Book preview shows career totals, split bests and the progression list from fictional results.

pitch.benefit: Browse another athlete’s published history while your own Locker stays unchanged.
pitch.problem: Looking up a teammate often means losing your place in your own results.
pitch.advantage: Explore keeps public athlete profiles read-only and separate from the Locker.
pitch.proof: The literal Explore screen shows a separate search entry point that does not claim another athlete.

pitch.benefit: Find a filmed pointer from Pattie or browse the library for the part of race day on your mind.
pitch.problem: Short practical reminders are easy to forget among long race checklists.
pitch.advantage: Ask Pattie guides athletes to her own recorded clips, and the library works offline after download.
pitch.proof: The literal Tips screen shows the Ask Pattie and episode-library navigation with an optional Pattie Mode invitation.
